newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ebner says will assess Winterthur anew.
newsitem.headline: Ebner says will assess Winterthur anew.

text.p: The head of the investment trust that owns a major stake in Winterthur Insurance Co said a new assessment of the situation is needed now that Credit Suisse Group was apparently interested in the insurer.

"We bought Winterthur with a long-term perspective. But now a new constellation has set in," Martin Ebner, head of the BZ Group, which has an 18.3 percent stake in Winterthur, said in an interview with the Swiss newspaper SonntagsZeitung.

"Apparently Credit Suisse Group is also interested and that's why the Winterthur (share) price has risen in a short time from 800 to over 1,400 (Swiss) francs. One must now make a new assessment of the situation," he was also quoted as saying.
Credit Suisse Group said on Friday that it did not have a "strategic" stake in Winterthur, but rather that it held well below five percent through its investment funds and internal pension fund.

Ebner also said in the interview published on Sunday that he was not contemplating a sale of the Winterthur shares at current prices. But he noted that he now expected a share price increase of no more than than 20 percent per year.
He further stated in the interview that he could not rule out a takeover of Winterthur.

"The entry of Rueck (Swiss Reinsurance Co) served as a signal for me. I infer from the statements from the CS side that more Winterthur shares could be purchased through pension funds or its own resources or for the ally Commerzbank. I therefore cannot rule out a takeover," Ebner was quoted as saying.
The spotlight was on Winterthur last week after Ebner revealed to the media that Swiss Reinsurance held around five percent of Winterthur.

The revelation sparked a flurry of reactions from Winterthur, Swiss Re and Credit Suisse and analysts said speculation about a looming takeover bid for Winterthur looked set to become a fixture in the Swiss share market.
In addition to the Credit Suisse statement, Swiss Re on Friday confirmed that it had the stake of around five percent.
Winterthur chairman Peter Spaelti told Swiss radio that he had heard nothing about any possible takeover offer for his company from Swiss Re or allied banking group Credit Suisse.
Winterthur also said in a separate statement that its share register contained no shareholders with more than five percent of the company's shares.
